memory_candidates.content: In BimodalLogic (and likely any repo using this agent-system template), specs/archive/ is wholly excluded by .gitignore and files under it are never git-tracked (confirmed via git ls-files/git log returning empty). Any implementation task whose file_scope is an archived path cannot use git diff/git status for per-phase verification -- the edits are real and persist on disk but are invisible to git. Substitute a saved before/after file snapshot (plain diff) plus grep-count checks for every 'git diff shows N hunks' verification criterion. Also note: a line-based diff tool (git diff or plain diff) merges textually-adjacent changed lines into one reported hunk regardless of tracking status, so an 'N anchors' count and an 'N hunks' count can legitimately diverge when two anchors sit on adjacent lines.

Content-match editing discipline (never line-number locators) worked cleanly across a three-phase, eight-anchor plan that explicitly forbade re-deriving replacement text: re-reading each phase's own plan section immediately before editing, confirming each old_string by live grep before applying it, and running the plan's own named grep-count verification immediately after each edit caught zero drift and required zero re-location fallback, despite the source plan itself admitting its own seven-anchor closure sentence had been mis-stated by a prior dispatch.

sapience_notes.subject: diff tooling and adjacent-line edits
sapience_notes.value: A line-based diff tool (git diff or plain diff alike) merges two textually-adjacent changed lines into a single reported hunk, independent of whether the file is git-tracked. A plan's 'N distinct anchors implies N diff hunks' assumption can therefore be wrong by a small amount when two of the anchors sit on consecutive lines; verify anchor count by content-location grep, not by hunk count.
